correctness.rationale: Kernel dimension is invariant under \(B\mapsto PBQ\) using the bijection \(U\mapsto PUQ^{-T}\). For the rank-normal form of \(B\), the trailing \(k(r-t)\) entries of \(U\) are free, the lower-left block vanishes, and the leading \(t\times t\) block is symmetric, contributing \(t(t+1)/2\) dimensions. Rank-nullity gives the image rank. Proposition 5.3 of the primary source parametrizes all fixed-residue shortest lifts by one affine translate of this kernel, so the power-of-two count follows. Exhaustive finite replay independently verifies every binary \(B\) through size \(3\times3\).

value.rationale: The primary paper explicitly enumerates these kernels in its construction of all shortest embeddings and uses that search to discover twelve database-improving codes. A closed fiber-size formula gives the exact cost of this central search stage before any Lee-distance computation and shows that detailed entries of the appended binary block are irrelevant once its rank is known. The monotonic rank law gives an immediate structural comparison between residue embeddings and can guide which fibers are computationally expensive.
